rule_level_problems.problem: Neither 'short history' nor 'single joint' is encoded, and the rule has no guard against the chronic branch. Because the priority rule escalates on (active_condition Infective arthritis), any patient whose joint is warm, swollen, severely painful and stiff - including a long-standing polyarthritis flare that the page sends down the chronic arthritis path - is diagnosed probable septic arthritis and made Urgent. Adding (<= (onset ...) (time_ago N days)) on the pain and (snomed_concept "Monoarticular joint involvement" "finding") would restore the page's discriminators.

The house standard says fever is recorded as (active_condition (snomed_concept "Fever" "finding")) because it is a common symptom; if the patient's fever was captured that way the negation may not see it, and the gout branch fires despite fever. The same page also offers Temperature >= 38 as a measurable alternative.

rule_level_problems.problem: The flowchart is explicitly for the patient 'not needing urgent attention', but none of the non-urgent 'likely' rules excludes the urgent conditions. An injured patient with severe swelling or deformity gets probable sprain/strain alongside probable fracture; a patient matching septic arthritis also matches chronic or gonococcal arthritis if the other criteria line up. The page's branch order (red box first) is lost. Adding (no (active_condition X)) for Fracture of bone / Infective arthritis, or the equivalent negated findings, would restore it.

rule_level_problems.problem: The gout arm re-states the whole red-box criterion inline instead of referencing (active_condition (snomed_concept "Acute gout" "disorder")) as the septic arthritis and fracture arms do. Logically equivalent today, but any fix to the gout rule (e.g. the missing surgery/injection exclusions) must be made twice; and if active_condition were used, the flowchart (non-urgent) gout arm would wrongly become Urgent, so the duplication is a trade-off worth a comment rather than a defect.

The 'Manage and refer urgently' criteria 'known gout with chronic kidney disease' and 'suspected secondary gout (haematological malignancy)' are not checked for anywhere; they are referral (management) criteria and out of scope, but a clinician may want them raised as a priority, since the page puts them in the red box.

summary: The red box and the flowchart are both encoded with the right concepts, thresholds, directions and rule types, and the priority rule has the house (and complaint (or ...)) shape. The most consequential gap is the septic arthritis rule: 'short history' and 'single joint' are missing and nothing excludes the chronic branch, so a long-standing polyarthritis flare becomes probable septic arthritis and Urgent. Secondary problems: the red-box gout criterion omits the 'no surgery or injection into joint' exclusions, fever is negated as a clinical_finding where the house standard records it as an active_condition, and the non-urgent 'likely' rules do not exclude the urgent conditions, so fracture and sprain/strain fire together.
